newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore stocks end down, hit by corporate fears.
newsitem.headline: Singapore stocks end down, hit by corporate fears.

text.p: The Singapore stock market ended lower on Friday as institutional funds continued to flee the island in the face of a dull corporate and economic outlook, dealers said.

Selling of index-linked Cycle & Carriage, Fraser & Neave, Singapore Press Holding led the Straits Times Industrials Index to a 28-month low at 1,978.31. A last minute rebound in the prices lifted the index to end at 1,990.12, down 0.56 points.
Bearish technicals and concerns over blue chip soft drink F&N results fueled the selling, dealers said. "Confidence was shaken after Cerebos' disappointing results," one dealer said.
Earlier this week index-linked Cerebos disappointed with flat earnings for six months ended March 31, 1997 against expectations of double digit growth.
Newly-listed telephone cord maker Huan Hsin was active with over 6.4 million shares traded. It ended US$0.045, up at US$0.515 against its initial public offer at US$0.42.
Hong Kong-based Jardine Matheson rose US$0.30 to US$7.45 on renewed rumours of a relisting in Hong Kong despite earlier denials from company officials.
Malayan Banking shed S$0.90 to S$14.60 on worries of Malaysia's curbs on swap trading.
